done_when: Every Forge repo's AGENTS.md tells agents to file a Forge bug with the bug template, and the template asks for everything needed to reproduce and fix it without any client code, names or secrets

known.title: Not done: Forge bug reports do not use the bug template
Not done: proof that the bug template retains required prompts

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. AGENTS.md directs agents to use the Forge bug template, but the guide tells them to create their own body file and submit it with `--body-file`. That command does not select the GitHub template; [GitHub CLI documents `--template` separately](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_issue_create). The copied instructions also omit the operating system requested by the template, so following the guide can produce a report without that reproduction detail.
findings.title: Not done: Forge bug reports do not use the bug template

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Test. The named proof derives its expected headings from the template and checks only their count and presence in the guide. Removing the template's prompts for the prior Forge version, relevant settings, operating system, or exclusion of client secrets would leave this test green, although those details are central to the Done-when requirement.
findings.title: Not done: proof that the bug template retains required prompts

why: When a coding agent hits a Forge bug in a client repo, nothing tells it to report the bug to Forge, so the Forge team learns late and without the details needed to fix it
